name: Eating disorder recovery

card.summary: The process of recovering from an eating disorder, which researchers say lacks a single agreed definition but typically spans physical, behavioural and psychological change.
card.note: Clinical topic; community posts about it sit alongside looksmaxxing diet and leanness discussion.

quick.overview:
Eating disorder recovery refers to the process of getting better from conditions such as anorexia nervosa, bulimia nervosa and binge eating disorder. Researchers say there are almost as many definitions of recovery as there are studies, but there is a trend towards including physical, behavioural and psychological components.

In looksmaxxing forums, posts about recovery appear alongside discussion of leanness, restriction and self-improvement, where some members describe returning to regular eating as part of a wider personal reset.
quick.mechanism: Treatment varies by disorder and can include counselling, dietary guidance, reducing excessive exercise and food avoidance, medication for associated symptoms, and hospitalisation in serious cases. Research on recovery highlights social support, social identity and perfectionism as factors.
quick.risks: Wikipedia reports that about 70% of people with anorexia nervosa and 50% with bulimia recover within five years, while only about 10% of people with eating disorders receive treatment. Both anorexia and bulimia increase the risk of death.

lead: Eating disorder recovery is the process of improving from an eating disorder. Researchers note that conceptually it should include physical, behavioural and psychological components, but this has not been applied consistently across studies [2][3]. A review described a long-standing problem that there are almost as many definitions of recovery as studies, with a general shift towards counting psychological and cognitive symptoms [3].

Treatment varies by disorder and may include counselling, dietary guidance, reducing excessive exercise and food-avoidance behaviours, medication for associated symptoms and hospitalisation in severe cases [1]. According to Wikipedia, about 70% of people with anorexia nervosa and about 50% with bulimia recover within five years, binge eating disorder recovery is estimated at 20% to 60%, and only about 10% of people with eating disorders receive treatment [1].
The topic appears in looksmaxxing communities, where leanness and diet are common subjects and some members post about recovering their eating.
infobox: Recovery from anorexia, bulimia, binge eating disorder and related conditions
Counselling, dietary guidance, medication for symptoms, hospitalisation if severe

paras: A study guided by theory identified a 'fully recovered' group using body mass index, absence of eating disorder behaviours and a psychological questionnaire, and compared them with partially recovered groups on psychosocial functioning and comorbidity [2]. A systematic review and qualitative meta-analysis found that recovered individuals emphasise criteria related to positive functioning, with no clear consensus on which additional criteria are most fundamental [4].

Studies of recovered individuals examine social support [5] and social identity, including the role of group identification in recovery [7]. Research has also looked at perfectionism across stages of recovery [6]. A study of people with lived experience described effects of the COVID-19 pandemic and UK lockdown on eating disorder recovery [8].

Studies are largely observational and qualitative, covering how recovery is defined and measured [2][3][4], social support [5], perfectionism [6] and social identity [7]. This overview does not summarise randomised treatment trials.

Some looksmax.org members post about recovery, for example one user describing a move from very low calorie intake back to eating again, alongside quitting substances and starting to exercise, and receiving congratulations from other members [9].

lore.intro: Recovery is not a core looksmaxxing topic, but members sometimes describe it as part of a personal reset [9].

claims.claim: Returning to regular eating and quitting vices is part of 'taking your life back'
claims.believers: A forum user described increasing food intake from a very low level towards maintenance alongside exercise and social connection, and others congratulated him [9].
claims.experts: Researchers define recovery as including physical, behavioural and psychological components and note that definitions vary widely [2][3].
